title: The two sailings nobody markets to you.
subtitle: Repositioning voyages and back-to-backs - the quiet end of the brochure.

text: The best weeks at sea are the ones with no marketing budget.
sub: A ship has to move between seasons whether anyone books it or not. When it does, it sails long and slow, with a run of sea days no brochure knows how to sell.

items.head: The flights, honestly
items.body: A one-way voyage means an open-jaw air booking. Price that before you fall for the fare.

items.head: The turnaround day
items.body: On a back-to-back you stay aboard whilst the ship empties. Ask what that day looks like - it can be the best one.

items.head: Whether the two loops overlap
items.body: Consecutive weeks often repeat two ports. Sometimes welcome; check that you'd want them twice.

items.head: The clock
items.body: Crossing eastbound, ship's time typically advances an hour a night. All-aboard is always ship's time.

points.label: Days 1 - 3
points.value: Coastal calls whilst the ship lets go of its summer season.

points.label: Days 4 - 9
points.value: Open ocean. The reading, the long dinners, the actual reason to go.

points.label: The clocks
points.value: Advanced about an hour a night eastbound. All-aboard is in ship's time.

points.label: Final days
points.value: Landfall calls, then a slow arrival into the new season's home port.

quote: A repositioning voyage isn't a lesser sailing. It's the same ship, with the marketing turned off.
